study.comments: Conference chapter (Plenum Press, 1991). Only topical imidazoles tested (bifonazole, econazole, oxiconazole); no standard and no breakpoints, so no S/I/R categorisation. MIC distribution per species given (Tables 2 and 3) but the OCR column alignment is poor; only the bifonazole values (both isolates at 10 µg/mL, the top concentration) are unambiguous. Methods state concentrations in mg/ml whereas tables use µg/ml. Text says 160 Candida-positive specimens but Table 1 totals 40 Candida isolates; n_candida_total taken from Table 1. Collection period not stated.

study.comments: S/SDD/R counts by agent for 39 C. tropicalis given in Table 1, but interpretive criteria (CLSI version) are not identified and no individual MICs or MIC distribution are reported (only range, MIC50, MIC90), so IC8 is not met. High azole resistance in C. tropicalis: FLC R 25.6%, VRC R 20.5%; 8 C. tropicalis cross-resistant to fluconazole and voriconazole; 12.8% (≈5 isolates) co-resistant to three azoles. Abstract gives C. albicans as 34.9% vs 33.8% in results (inconsistency not affecting C. tropicalis).

clade4.note: No genotyping, although the high azole resistance in C. tropicalis from China is compatible with the context in which the resistant clade has been described.

study.comments: Number of C. tropicalis from periodontitis patients is 3 in abstract and Table 1 but 2 in the Methods text; 3 used. Authors report that no C. tropicalis isolate was resistant to any drug (resistant isolates were only C. albicans, C. glabrata and Candida spp.). Breakpoints leave gaps (e.g. FLC 32, KTC 8) that are neither S nor R; MIC ranges reach those values, so n_S is not derivable. Periodontitis Table 1 inconsistency for C. tropicalis: ketoconazole and miconazole MIC90 (8) exceed the reported range maximum (4). Collection period not stated (published 2004).

study.comments: Combination study; no S/I/R categorisation by the authors. Single-drug MICs taken from the 'alone' columns; micafungin alone MICs differ slightly between panels (0.015–0.03 with FLCZ, 0.03–0.06 with VRCZ/AMPH-B, 0.03 with 5-FC); reported row uses the AMPH-B panel. Out-of-range isolates excluded from combination analysis (6 for FLCZ, 2 for VRCZ).

Discussion says 'only two C. tropicalis strains and one strain was susceptible' (to azoles). Period April 2020–April 2024.
